full_judgment:
A. M. Mahmudur Rahman, J.: By this Rule the pre-emptor petitioner calls in question the judgment and order dated 29.11.84 passed by Miss Nasreen Begum, Munsir, Dhamrai Upazila, Dhaka, in Misc case No. 35 of 1983 allowing the Mise. Case No. 101 of 1981 setting aside an ex-parte order made in a pre-emption case under section 96 of the State Acquisition & Tenancy Act restoring the same to its file and number. 

 2. Mr. Abdus Salam Khan submits that the opposite party No. 1 was opposite party No 4 in the aforesaid pre-emption case and he was served with the notice of that case. He did not, after service of notice, appear before the court and take any step, but all on a sudden on 28.2.83 he filed the Misc. Case No. 35 of 1983 for setting aside the ex-parte order made in the pre-emption case on 29.4.82 on The allegation that he came to know about the ex-parte order from the peon of the Court who went to locality to give delivery of possession of the land to the pre-emptor. Mr. Salam further submits that although the opposite party No. I alleged his definite knowledge about the ex-parte order on 27.2.83 from the information slip, he failed to prove his knowledge from such information slip. On the face of such circumstances and facts, the learned Munsif most illegally, without arriving at a finding that the opposite party had knowledge from 27.3.83 held that the Misc. Case No 35 of 1983 was filed-within time. Mr. Salam Khan submits that Article 164 of the Limitation Act provides 30 days for filing an application for setting aside an ex-parte order. In this case the definite case of opposite party No.1 was that he had knowledge from the information slip about the ex-parte order which was made on 29.4.82. As the opposite party No. 1 failed to prove his knowledge from 27.2.83 by evidence, the learned Munsif, contrary to the provision of Article 164 of the Limitation Act, passed the impugned order. Mr. Abdus Salam Khan, further submits that from order No. 56 dated 5.2.84 it also appears that the process of the pre-emption case was served on the notice/or summons is served on a party and he asserts his 'knowledge from source other than from the service of notice and denies the service of notice, he is under legal obligation to prove that the case for setting aside the ex-parte decree or order is made within 30 days as provided under Article 164 of the Limitation Act. Failure to prove such knowledge disentitled party to get the benefit of Order 9, Rule 13 C.P.C. and on the ground of limitation the proceeding under Order 9, Rule 13 is liable to be dismissed. The learned Advocate for the petitioner, inviting my attention to a Order No.4 as well as Order No. 56, submits that the notice was served, but it appears that the same was not available on record. It is true that in absence of any evidence to show that the notice was served on the opposite party No. 1, it cannot be held that he had such knowledge of service of notice. But where he denies service of notice and makes on his case from the date of his knowledge from other source, he is to prove that the case is filed within 30 days of such knowledge. But in this case it has not been so proved. In this case, in view of failure by the opposite party No. 1 to prove his knowledge from the information slip, the learned Advocate of the opposite party was unable to support the impugned order. However, he made an attempt to argue that for ends of justice, the order impugned should not be disturbed. I am afraid to accept the contention in view of the facts and circumstances of the case as stated earlier.
